lines: \subsection{Robustness to Non-Independence}
\label{sec:robustness_method}

-The 455 panels share judges combinatorially (each appears in 91 panels), inducing correlated residuals. We correct for this using clustered standard errors (CR1, 3-position max-SE), mixed-effects models (random judge intercepts, 3-position max-$p$), and wild cluster bootstrap ($B{=}9{,}999$, Rademacher weights, 3-position max-$p$) following \citet{cameron2008bootstrap}. The 13 clusters per position at $K{=}3$ are below the ${\geq}20$ threshold recommended by \citet{cameron2008bootstrap}; at $K{=}5$, cluster count drops to ${\leq}11$, and at $K{=}7$ to ${\leq}9$. Following \citet{mackinnon2018wild}, we use Rademacher weights, which remain conservative in few-cluster settings even when cluster sizes are unequal. The bootstrap attenuation at $K{=}3$ (4/12 significant) may partly reflect insufficient cluster count rather than absent effects. Under the most demanding correction for crossed judge membership (multi-membership CRVE with $t(14)$ distribution), $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ retains 8/12 significance at $K{\geq}5$; the $K{=}3$ attenuation (0/12 vs.\ bootstrap 4/12) reflects the conservative degrees of freedom rather than absent effects (Appendix~\ref{app:crossed_re}). We use the log-log specification rather than fractional response models \citep{papke1996econometric} or beta regression \citep{ferrari2004beta} because the log transform linearizes the multiplicative $K_{\mathrm{eff}} \cdot \eta_{\max}$ structure; fractional logit with clustered SE serves as an $\epsilon$-free robustness check (Appendix~\ref{app:robustness_checks}). Details are in Appendix~\ref{app:robustness_methods}.

\label{sec:robustness_method}

-The 455 panels share judges combinatorially (each appears in 91 panels), inducing correlated residuals. We correct for this using clustered standard errors (CR1, 3-position max-SE), mixed-effects models (random judge intercepts, 3-position max-$p$), and wild cluster bootstrap ($B{=}9{,}999$, Rademacher weights, 3-position max-$p$) following \citet{cameron2008bootstrap}. The 13 clusters per position at $K{=}3$ are below the ${\geq}20$ threshold recommended by \citet{cameron2008bootstrap}; at $K{=}5$, cluster count drops to ${\leq}11$, and at $K{=}7$ to ${\leq}9$. Following \citet{mackinnon2018wild}, we use Rademacher weights, which remain conservative in few-cluster settings even when cluster sizes are unequal. The bootstrap attenuation at $K{=}3$ (4/12 significant) may partly reflect insufficient cluster count; under crossed random effects correction (multi-membership CRVE, $t(14)$; Appendix~\ref{app:crossed_re}), $K_{\mathrm{eff}}$ retains 8/12 at $K{\geq}5$ while $K{=}3$ attenuates further (0/12). 10	Multi-judge panels have emerged as the dominant defense against bias and manipulation in LLM-based evaluation. 11	
12	Yet the evidence for diversity as a causal defense is weaker than it appears. 14	In our experiments, we observe a panel-size-dependent predictor shift.
